proposals: ICAR-CRRI should publish the plot-level methane measurements and the AWD water-management protocol from its two-year trial with BASF in Odisha and Jharkhand when it ends, so the emission cuts can be checked independently of any company that hopes to sell credits from them.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare should keep a public register of corporate rice-carbon programmes in India, listing sponsors, states, farmers and hectares enrolled, the standard used and credits issued, so programmes such as TGRA's 10,000-plus farmers can be followed from enrolment to issuance.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency should state whether AWD-based rice credits are eligible under India's domestic carbon market and, if so, which remote-sensing verification it will require, given that Verra invalidated 99.9% of the rice credits it had ever issued.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare should issue model terms for farmer enrolment in rice-carbon programmes, setting out how credit revenue is shared and who bears the cost if credits are later invalidated, so smallholders are not left exposed to a repeat of the 2024 Verra review.
